question: Can the identity-admission component reject inconsistent citation packets while retaining valid identity matches and leaving semantic support unreviewed?
scope_change: The broad scenario includes semantic support. This first run tests only document/paragraph/edition/payload consistency and uncertainty preservation. It is an engineering feasibility comparison, not the H1 reviewer study or theological evaluation.
sampling: Purposive finite category-coverage design; no random sampling, hidden holdout, power or general reliability estimate.
independence: One AI assistant authored code and fixture expectations. No independent human or theological labels. Expectations arise from seeded mutations and explicit positive construction, not model evaluation.

arms.simple_checklist: Short-circuit function of the same identity prerequisites; primary comparator.
arms.structured_gate: Per-dimension match/mismatch/unknown states; same information and criteria.
arms.locator_diagnostic: Adaptation of legacy derive() literal reference comparison. Diagnostic ablation only, not a source-admission policy or existing institutional deployment.

prerequisites: document and paragraph in both pointers
no conflicting ID binding in retained search
normalization: UTF-8, Unicode NFC and collapsed whitespace for synthetic body; paragraph accepts digits or para- digits. URL parser allows HTTPS www.magisterium.com, no credentials, no non-443 port. No fuzzy document or paragraph matching.
support_rule: All arms return semantic_support=unreviewed and answer_verified=false. Identity admissibility is never theological truth or permission to publish an answer.
metrics: locator positives on inadmissible cases labelled misleading signals, not actual admissions
execution: One complete local pass per procedure on identical case membership/order; no network/model calls, retries, tuning, post-run exclusions or claims of measured human time/cost.
stop_rules: Any exception, failed input hash or malformed required record stops the run and is preserved.
Do not relabel or remove failed cases. Amend or fix under a distinct run only.
Any difference between checklist and gate is reported and investigated, not auto-corrected.
limits: A successful finite test is not independent validation, a provider defect finding, user benefit, field performance, doctrinal approval or CEC superiority.
Synthetic reference payloads are invented; original Vatican bytes are not claimed to be tested.
The archived replays have no public full passage bytes and are not new live observations.
expected_reference_origin: Assistant-authored development oracle; not an independent gold standard.
code_revision_before_execution: GitHub plan commit to be recorded in the run receipt; inputs identified above by hashes.
